next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — 2026 Voting Schedule

glance_notes.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — 2026 Voting Schedule
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Ohio's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5. County boards of elections and the Ohio Secretary of State's office are open until 9:00 p.m. that day.

glance_notes.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — 2026 Voting Schedule
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 6–November 1: Ohio's in-person early-voting period for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins October 6 and ends November 1. Statewide early-voting hours are established by law and include the two Saturdays and the Sunday immediately before Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voter ID Requirements
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required: Ohio voters casting an in-person ballot must generally present an acceptable, unexpired photo ID showing the voter's name and photograph. Ohio driver's licenses, Ohio state identification cards, U.S. passports and passport cards, and specified military and veterans identification are among the accepted forms.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Ohio residents may register online through the Ohio Secretary of State, submit a voter registration form by mail or register in person through a county board of elections and other authorized locations. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on or before the next General Election, have been an Ohio resident for at least 30 days immediately before the election and meet Ohio's other voter eligibility requirements. Eligible 17-year-olds who will be 18 by the General Election may vote in a Primary Election to nominate candidates, although they cannot vote on questions and issues at that Primary. A person convicted of a felony may register and vote after release from incarceration if otherwise eligible.
register.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Ohio requires registration at least 30 days before an election. Current Ohio eligibility rules permit voting after release from incarceration for a felony conviction; probation or parole alone does not prevent an otherwise eligible person from registering. Ohio's age rule permits certain 17-year-olds to participate in candidate-nomination portions of a Primary if they will turn 18 by the General Election.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Ohio Secretary of State's official voter lookup or your county board of elections to confirm that your voter registration is current. Voters should verify their address before Election Day because the registered residence determines the voter's precinct and assigned Election Day polling location.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the Secretary of State or county board
check_registration.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voter Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: Ohio's statewide voter resources direct voters to county-specific voter lookup systems. County boards maintain voter records and are the authoritative local source if a registration record or address appears incorrect.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Ohio requires eligible residents to register at least 30 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the voter registration deadline is Monday, October 5. County boards of elections and the Ohio Secretary of State's office remain open until 9:00 p.m. on the deadline. Ohio does not provide general same-day voter registration during early voting or on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — 2026 Voting Schedule
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Ohio Elections Calendar and current voting schedule directly establish October 5 as the General Election registration deadline under R.C. 3503.19. Because the 30th day before Election Day falls on Sunday, October 4, the deadline moves to Monday, October 5 under Ohio's deadline rules.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: On Election Day, Ohio voters must cast their ballot at the polling place assigned to their precinct based on their registered residential address. Use the Ohio Secretary of State's polling-place lookup or contact your county board of elections to find the correct location. A voter who appears at the wrong polling location may be directed to the correct location or may need to use a provisional ballot under Ohio law. Early voting takes place at locations designated by the county board of elections rather than at ordinary Election Day precinct polling places.
polling_place.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Polling Location
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Election FAQ explicitly states that Election Day voters must vote in their precinct at the designated polling place. County boards establish polling locations and early-voting sites. Locations should be rechecked close to Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Ohio's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. A voter who is in line by 7:30 p.m. has the right to vote. In-person voters generally must present an acceptable, unexpired photo ID showing their name and photograph. A voter who does not have acceptable identification may cast a provisional ballot and provide qualifying identification to the county board of elections during the post-election cure period.
election_day.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voting in Ohio
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 voting schedule confirms November 3 and 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. polling hours. The Secretary of State confirms that voters in line by 7:30 p.m. may vote. Ohio's current photo-ID law applies to in-person voting, with provisional-ballot and cure procedures available when required identification is not presented.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Ohio polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone who is waiting in line at 7:30 p.m. must be allowed to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Election FAQ
polling_hours.internal_note: Ohio's statewide Election Day polling hours are uniform. The Secretary of State's current FAQ directly confirms 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. and the right of voters already in line at closing to vote.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Ohio provides in-person early voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins October 6 and ends November 1. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. October 6-9, October 12-16 and October 19-23; 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. October 24; 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. October 26; 7:30 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. October 27; 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. October 28-30; 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. October 31; and 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. November 1. Early voting is administered through county boards of elections.
early_voting.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — 2026 Voting Schedule
early_voting.internal_note: The Ohio Secretary of State has already published the complete statewide early-voting schedule for the November 3, 2026 General Election. There is no early in-person voting on Monday, November 2. Ohio's schedule includes the two Saturdays and the Sunday immediately before Election Day.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any qualified Ohio voter may vote absentee by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee voting by mail begins October 6. A completed absentee-ballot application must be received by the voter's county board of elections by 8:30 p.m. on October 27. Non-military and non-overseas absentee ballots must be received by the county board of elections no later than 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. A ballot returned by mail is not counted merely because it was postmarked by Election Day; it must arrive by the Election Day receipt deadline. A voter or qualifying near relative may hand-deliver a completed ballot to the county board, and counties provide secure ballot drop boxes under Ohio's return procedures.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; request by 8:30 p.m. October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Request an Absentee Ballot
absentee_mail.internal_note: IMPORTANT 2026 rule: current Ohio law requires all non-UOCAVA absentee ballots to be RECEIVED by 7:30 p.m. Election Day. Older Ohio guidance describing a postmark-before-Election-Day rule with post-election receipt is outdated. The official 2026 voting schedule establishes October 6 as the beginning of absentee voting, October 27 at 8:30 p.m. as the application deadline and November 3 at 7:30 p.m. as the non-UOCAVA receipt deadline.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Ohio voters casting an in-person ballot generally must show a valid, unexpired photo ID containing the voter's name and photograph. Accepted identification includes an Ohio driver's license, State of Ohio identification card or qualifying interim identification form; a U.S. passport or passport card; a U.S. military identification card or military dependent identification card; an Ohio National Guard identification card; or a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs identification card. An Ohio driver's license or state identification card may show a previous address as long as the voter's current residential address is correctly recorded with the Board of Elections. Utility bills, bank statements, government checks, paychecks and out-of-state driver's licenses are not accepted as voter identification for ordinary in-person voting.
voter_id.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State voter-ID page provides the authoritative accepted-ID list. Ohio Mobile ID is currently not accepted. A driver's license or identification card issued by another state is not acceptable. A voter without qualifying photo ID may vote provisionally and cure the identification deficiency under Ohio's post-election procedures. Ohio also provides a religious-objection affidavit procedure for qualifying voters with sincerely held religious objections to being photographed.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Ohio provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. Polling locations and early-voting sites must provide accessible voting opportunities, and voters may receive assistance when needed. Ohio also provides a remote ballot-marking system for absentee voters with qualifying disabilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, allowing the voter to access and mark an absentee ballot using compatible assistive technology. The ballot must then be returned according to Ohio's absentee-ballot procedures. Voters who experience an accessibility problem may contact their county board of elections or the Ohio Secretary of State.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible in-person and remote ballot-marking options
accessible_voting.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voting Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State confirms accessible in-person and absentee voting and a remote ballot-marking system for qualifying absentee voters with disabilities. Current 2026 election forms include Form 11-G for requesting the remote ballot-marking system and Form 12-N containing instructions. The remote system assists with receiving and marking the ballot and should not be described as unrestricted online voting.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Ohio provides special voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when applicable. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, military and overseas absentee voting begins September 18. Qualifying UOCAVA ballots returned by mail must be received by the appropriate county board of elections no later than November 7 to be counted under Ohio's current 2026 election calendar. Military and overseas voters should follow Ohio's dedicated UOCAVA instructions because their ballot-delivery and return rules differ from ordinary domestic absentee voting.
military_overseas.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 election schedule establishes September 18 as the UOCAVA ballot-availability date and November 7 as the receipt deadline for qualifying UOCAVA ballots returned by mail. Ohio permits electronic transmission of UOCAVA ballots to voters, including email delivery, but ballot-return requirements must follow Ohio law and the specific UOCAVA instructions. Do not apply the November 3 domestic absentee receipt deadline to all UOCAVA ballots.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Ohio if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student may establish an Ohio college residence as the place the student intends to make a permanent residence for voting purposes, or may retain another qualifying voting residence. Students should register and vote from only one residence in an election. A student who votes in person in Ohio must comply with Ohio's photo-ID requirement; student identification cards are not accepted as voter identification under Ohio's current voter-ID law.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may use one qualifying residence; student IDs are not voter ID
student_voting.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voter Information
student_voting.internal_note: Ohio's general residency rules apply to college students. The current voter-ID law is especially important for students: college or university student IDs are not on Ohio's accepted voter-ID list. An otherwise eligible student voting in person must present one of the accepted Ohio, federal, passport, military or VA photo IDs. The reader-facing language avoids claiming that merely attending an Ohio college automatically establishes voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Ohio voters can obtain voter-specific sample-ballot information through their county board of elections and the Secretary of State's voter resources. Ballot contents depend on the voter's precinct and local districts. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Secretary of State certified the form of official ballots to county boards by August 25. Voters should use their county's official voter lookup or sample-ballot system to review the ballot that applies to their registered address after local ballot preparation is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check your county board for your sample ballot
sample_ballot.source_name: Ohio Secretary of State — Voter Information
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official 2026 Elections Calendar establishes August 25 as the deadline for the Secretary of State to certify the form of official General Election ballots to boards of elections. County boards provide voter-specific sample ballots and ballot lookup services. Because local candidate and issue details vary by precinct, voters should use county-specific official resources rather than a generic statewide sample.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Ohio Secretary of State, Elections Division, 22 North Fourth Street, 15th Floor, Columbus, OH 43215. Phone: 614-466-2655. Toll-free: 877-SOS-OHIO (877-767-6446). TTY: 614-466-0562. Toll-free TTY: 877-644-6889. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, absentee-ballot or early-voting questions, contact your county board of elections.
contact.internal_note: The current Secretary of State election pages verify 614-466-2655, 877-767-6446, 614-466-0562 and 877-644-6889. County boards of elections administer voter-specific local election functions. No unverified general elections email address was inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Ohio Secretary of State's VoteOhio.gov resources for official statewide election information. The site provides voter registration, registration lookup, polling-place information, voter identification requirements, absentee voting, early-voting schedules, military and overseas voting resources and county board of elections contacts. County boards administer voter registration records, polling places, early voting, absentee ballots and other voter-specific election functions.
